structure.title: A story on the Thames
structure.text: An outer narrator introduces Marlow's account. The European listening place remains part of the story's moral geography.

structure.title: Moving upriver
structure.text: Delays, stations, and reports accumulate around Kurtz. Marlow's desire to understand depends on information supplied by interested observers.

people.name: Marlow
people.text: A seaman on a boat in the Thames at dusk, telling his companions about a voyage he once made up a great African river.

people.name: Kurtz
people.text: An ivory agent deep in the interior, spoken of with awe by everyone Marlow meets, whom Marlow becomes more and more anxious to reach.

people.name: The Company
people.text: The Belgian trading company that hires Marlow to captain a river steamer, and whose stations along the river he sees for himself.

context.title: Extraction and civilisation
context.text: The company's stated ideals coexist with violence and extraction. Its euphemisms matter because they organise what employees can ignore.

context.title: A restricted viewpoint
context.text: African people are often filtered through Marlow's language rather than given equivalent narrative authority. Criticism of empire does not remove that limitation.
context.takeaway: Notice whose interior life remains unavailable.

notice.text: Follow the making of Kurtz's reputation.
notice.why: Fascination can grow before evidence becomes available.

notice.text: Notice breaks and qualifications in Marlow's telling.
notice.why: Difficulty of description becomes part of the subject.

opening: Marlow takes a job piloting a steamer into the Congo, where a European trading company speaks of civilisation and measures success in ivory. The farther he travels, the harder those two descriptions become to reconcile. Everyone talks about Kurtz, an exceptional agent whose results seem to excuse almost anything. Conrad builds the journey out of delays, rumours, and glimpses of violence, making the desire to meet this remarkable man entangle the reader in the same fascination that has helped protect him from scrutiny.
